title: Strict localizations are invariant under ind-etale morphisms
statement:
Let $u:T\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] which is ind-etale locally on source and target: near each point of $T$, choose affine opens $\operatorname{Spec}B\subset T$ and $\operatorname{Spec}A\subset S$ such that $u$ maps the first into the second and $B$ is a filtered colimit of etale $A$-algebras of finite presentation [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra]. For every geometric point $t:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to T$ [def-weil-geometric-point], with $s=u(t)$ defined using the same field $\Omega$, the canonical functorial map of strict localizations [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-functoriality]
$$T_{(t)}\longrightarrow S_{(s)}$$
is an isomorphism over $S$. Strict localizations have the inverse-limit construction of [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit]. The assertion applies after arbitrary scheme base change [def-pc-fibre-product] of $u$ and includes the canonical structural map [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-structural-map] of a strict localization, localized again at its closed geometric point.

proof.text: Choose the local affine opens V and U at the image of the geometric point. Present them by spectra of their global sections using isoSpec, and use proAffineEtale_iff_appTop to make the ring map ind-etale. Composition with the canonical ULift ring equivalences gives its IndEtaleAcrossUniverses formulation. Take h to be Spec.preimage of the canonical strictHenselizationMap; Spec.map_preimage fixes its spectrum exactly. Apply [lem-trf-strict-local-comparison-ind-etale], choose the two chart factorizations, and use its universal clause to obtain ind-etaleness of h, strict henselianity of both rings, and locality of h. The ind-etale-implies-weakly-etale clause of [lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-stability] is already proved separately upstream as RingHom.IndEtale.weaklyEtale; apply it to the ULift transport and descend weak etaleness using Algebra.WeaklyEtale.ulift_iff. Olivier [thm-weil-pbc-weak-etale-strict-local] makes h bijective, so its ring equivalence gives an isomorphism on spectra [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Its spectrum is the chosen canonical map, with the structural and evaluation equations of [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-functoriality], on the unchanged small strict-localization model [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit].

proof.text: For an arbitrary g:S′→S, apply the final clause of [lem-trf-locally-ind-etale-base-change-charts] to the spectrum presentations obtained in step 1. This supplies the same local spectrum chart hypothesis for the second projection T×_S S′→S′. Apply the already proved chart-to-isomorphism argument at any geometric point of the pullback. Package its canonical map with its structural and evaluation equations as the required isomorphism. No extra condition is imposed on g or on the geometric field.

source.place: Tag 01JR, lemma-open-fibre-product; Tag 01I4, lemma-fibre-product-affine-schemes; Tag 01JQ, lemma-fibre-product-affines; Tag 097J, lemma-base-change-ind-etale. Synthesis of the returned parent proof, step 4.

proof.text: Write s for the original image geometric point. Choose a spectrum open chart iU:Spec A→S containing its image, and apply [lem-trf-strict-local-comparison-ind-etale] to id_S, s, this same chart on both sides, and id_A, which is ind-etale. The factorization clause and the universal clause give a:A→H_S ind-etale with Spec(a)≫iU=j_S, where j_S is [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-structural-map]. Put t=Spec(strictHenselizationPointEvaluation s). Its composite with j_S is s by strictHenselizationClosedLift_over, the geometric-point factorization in [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-functoriality]. Thus iU and the identity chart Spec H_S→Spec H_S satisfy the chart hypothesis for j_S at t. Apply the same chart-to-isomorphism argument once more. This proves IsIso of precisely the canonical strictHenselizationMap j_S t, without replacing it by an arbitrary isomorphism.

lean.statement: theorem indEtale_strictLocal_invariance {S T : Scheme.{u}} (u : T ⟶ S) (hlocal : ∀ (t : T), ∃ (V : T.Opens) (U : S.Opens), t ∈ V ∧ IsAffine V.toScheme ∧ IsAffine U.toScheme ∧ ∃ e : V.toScheme ⟶ U.toScheme, e ≫ U.ι = V.ι ≫ u ∧ proAffineEtale e) : ∀ {Ω : Type u} [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω] (barT : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ T) (barS : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ S) (hbar : barS = barT ≫ u), ∃ e : strictHenselizationScheme barT ≅ strictHenselizationScheme barS, e.hom ≫ strictHenselizationStructuralMap barS = strictHenselizationStructuralMap barT ≫ u ∧ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (strictHenselizationPointEvaluation barT)) ≫ e.hom = Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (strictHenselizationPointEvaluation barS)) ∧ (∀ (S' : Scheme.{u}) (g : S' ⟶ S) {Ω' : Type u} [Field Ω'] [IsAlgClosed Ω'] (barT' : Spec (.of Ω') ⟶ pullback u g), ∃ e' : strictHenselizationScheme barT' ≅ strictHenselizationScheme (barT' ≫ pullback.snd u g), e'.hom ≫ strictHenselizationStructuralMap (barT' ≫ pullback.snd u g) = strictHenselizationStructuralMap barT' ≫ pullback.snd u g ∧ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (strictHenselizationPointEvaluation barT')) ≫ e'.hom = Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (strictHenselizationPointEvaluation (barT' ≫ pullback.snd u g)))) ∧ IsIso (strictHenselizationMap (strictHenselizationStructuralMap barS) (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (strictHenselizationPointEvaluation barS))))
